Car crashes into crowd in Australia, 10 injured

A driver lost control and crashed his car into a crowd of rugby league fans in the eastern Australian city of Newcastle on Saturday, injuring 10 people including children, police said. Thousands of supporters had gathered to farewell local rugby league side the Newcastle Knights ahead of their grand final match against the Sydney Roosters on Sunday. But the festive environment was shattered when an 18-year-old rugby fan “driving erratically” lost control of his vehicle and crashed into the crowd

corpus.title: Five-year-old girl in critical condition after car hits crowd in Newcastle
corpus.signal_text:
Ten people have been injured, one critically, after a car crashed into a crowd of people in Newcastle waiting to farewell the Knights team bus before the NRL grand final.
New South Wales police said a five-year-old girl remained in a critical condition after the crash on Saturday morning.
Initially a 67-year-old man was also in a critical. The man is now in a serious but stable condition.
John Hunter hospital provided an update to Australian Associated Press on Saturday night confirming five other patients were in a stable condition and three others had been discharged.
The injured were treated on the scene by NSW ambulance paramedics, before being taken to hospital.
The P-plate driver was an 18-year-old man who was arrested at the scene and taken to hospital for mandatory testing, police said.
The assistant commissioner David Waddell said there were reports the man was driving erratically before losing control and careening into the crowd. It was expected he would be charged later on Saturday.
The man had two others in the car with him.
“We had to get them out of there because the crowd did turn on them,” Waddell said.
The police minister, Yasmin Catley, said so many lives had been affected by a split-second decision, as she urged other drivers to take care over the NSW long weekend.
“We have already started Saturday morning with this devastation,” she said.
“Nobody can comprehend what has happened with this terrible tragedy.”
The roads minister, Jenny Aitchison, said the incident could have been worse, with more than 1,000 people gathered in the area where it occurred.
Emergency services were called to Newcastle Link Road at the Transfield Drive roundabout in Wallsend about 9.30am on Saturday after reports a vehicle struck multiple people in a crowd.
“Several people have been injured and are currently receiving treatment at the scene,” police said.
“Police have commenced an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the incident, with initial inquiries indicating it is not believed to be terror related.”
Gavin Morris, the mayor of Newcastle, told the ABC that the driver, who he said was a Knights fan, lost control while revving his car shortly before the team arrived.

corpus.title: Ten people injured, P-plater charged after car crashes into Newcastle Knights fans
corpus.signal_text:
Ten people injured, P-plater charged after car crashes into Newcastle Knights fans
Updated ,first published
A five-year-old girl was left fighting for her life and nine others were injured when a teenage P-plate driver allegedly lost control of his car and careered into jubilant crowds lining a Newcastle street to wave the Knights off to the NRL grand final.
One of the injured, Chris Clancy, said the car appeared to speed up as it went through a roundabout, and then lost control on the wet road. “No-one had time to move,” he said. “I thought I was going to die, it happened so fast.”
Fans at the crash site rushed to provide first aid as emergency crews rushed to the scene and word of the collision spread through the tens of thousands of excited fans waiting for a glimpse of their team. The team’s bus, which had not yet departed when the crash occurred, was rerouted, and players were informed.
“They were shocked, it was a very sombre bus ride,” said one of those aboard. “Our fans mean everything to us. For that to happen; horrible.”
The five-year-old girl was in a critical condition in John Hunter Hospital on Saturday evening. One patient was in a serious but stable condition, and five were stable. Three had been discharged.
Police arrested the 18-year-old driver, Indika Bambrick Samarasinghe, at the crash site and took him for mandatory drug and alcohol testing. He was later charged with three counts each of dangerous driving occasioning grievous bodily harm, negligent driving occasioning grievous bodily harm and causing bodily harm by misconduct in charge of a motor vehicle. He was refused police bail to face a court on Sunday.
NSW Police Assistant Commissioner David Waddell said officers were investigating reports the P-plater had been “driving erratically” before he lost control of the vehicle.
Footage posted to social media depicted the BMW careering around the roundabout moments before the crash, as shocked onlookers were heard screaming. The driver is expected to be charged, but no charges had been laid at the time of publication.
Onlookers expressed anger towards the occupants of the car after the crash, police said. “We had to get the three of them out of there because the crowd did turn on them,” Waddell said.
Witness Dean Liddell said he could hear the vehicle coming towards the crowd and then “all hell broke loose”.
